overview: Sunday's news is dominated by a rising political row in India over Mallikarjun Kharge's remark on PM Modi, a fresh Election Commission transparency dispute, Israel and Brazil heading into close votes, and markets falling again as crude stays above $110.

items.headline: PM Modi inaugurates RBI data centre and cybersecurity institute in Odisha
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi opened the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre and a cybersecurity training institute in Odisha.
items.detail: Modi said financial institutions must be protected against cyber threats. The facilities are part of the RBI's technology and security setup.

items.headline: Netanyahu warns of nuclear threat ahead of Israel's election
items.summary: Israel votes in an election described as its most important in years, and Netanyahu has warned about Iran.
items.detail: Netanyahu said a nuclear threat would overshadow everything and warned Iran may try to disrupt the vote. He also posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv.

items.headline: Lula and Bolsonaro draw crowds on eve of tight Brazil runoff
items.summary: Brazilians vote in a close presidential runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro after election-eve rallies.
items.detail: Both camps held large rallies on the eve of the vote. Early reports point to a tight contest.

items.headline: Machado returns to Venezuela after nearly a year in exile
items.summary: Nobel laureate and opposition leader Maria Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela from exile.
items.detail: She said 'I am here. With you' on arrival, after almost a year away. Her return is being closely watched by Venezuelans and by governments abroad.

items.headline: Kharge's 'Modi ka baap bhi jayega' remark sparks row; BJP calls nationwide protest
items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's remark at a Patna event has led the BJP to demand an apology and call a nationwide demonstration.
items.detail: BJP leaders, including Amit Shah, say the remark abused PM Modi and his family, and Odisha's chief minister also criticised it. Congress says Kharge was responding to heckling and says the BJP and RSS have shown him disrespect. The row adds to an already heated week between the two parties.

items.headline: Election Commission cites trade secrets to deny RTI on SIR software
items.summary: The Election Commission has said software used in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls is exempt from RTI disclosure.
items.detail: The Commission says the software details are trade secrets, and says all its decisions, including SIR, are taken unanimously by the full Commission. Congress says the refusal to disclose ECINET details points to manipulation, and opposition parties are calling for more transparency.
items.why_it_matters: Voter-roll changes affect who can vote in the constituencies you and your family care about, so the transparency debate is worth following.

items.headline: Ex-judge says Chandrachud was too deferential to government; collegium stays unanimous, says ex-CJI
items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge SK Kaul has criticised ex-CJI Chandrachud's approach to appointments, while Chandrachud says collegium decisions are unanimous.
items.detail: Kaul says the collegium must resist pressure, and Congress has cited his memoir to question judicial independence under the Modi government. Chandrachud has said collegium decisions are unanimous. The collegium system is how senior judges are chosen for the higher judiciary.

items.headline: Schools shut in Andaman and Nicobar as cyclonic storm nears
items.summary: All schools in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands will stay closed on October 26 and 27 because of the approaching cyclonic storm.
items.detail: The disaster management directorate has told the public to stay alert as the Bay of Bengal depression is likely to strengthen. There is no new Great Nicobar project news in today's headlines.

items.headline: UNESCO adds Andaman volcanic landscapes to Tentative List
items.summary: UNESCO has added three Indian sites to its Tentative List, including Andaman volcanic landscapes.
items.detail: The Tentative List is the first formal step before a site can be nominated for World Heritage status. The other additions include Chhattisgarh's Sirpur, which features ancient temples.

items.headline: Goyal says developed nations have not paid the $100 billion climate promise
items.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal has said 'not a dime' has been received from developed nations toward the $100 billion climate promise.
items.detail: He made the point at a climate dialogue in Berlin, pressing rich countries on climate finance. Turkey hosts the next UN climate talks, COP31, and the finance gap is expected to be a central issue.

items.headline: IRDAI extends feedback window on distribution reforms; over 650 comments received
items.summary: The insurance regulator IRDAI has extended the deadline for comments on proposed distribution reforms to October 31.
items.detail: The regulator has received more than 650 comments so far. The reforms concern how insurance products are sold and how agents and intermediaries are paid.
items.why_it_matters: Broker commission and distribution rules in India shape how intermediaries work with insurers, which is relevant to your broker-facing role.

items.headline: Bahrain to make health insurance compulsory for resident expats from the 31st
items.summary: Bahrain's national health insurance scheme for resident expatriates will become compulsory, and it will also apply to private-sector expats.
items.detail: The headline gives the start date as the 31st without naming the month, so check the date before acting. The scheme covers expatriates across the private sector.
items.why_it_matters: A compulsory GCC expat health scheme changes the market for private medical insurance in the region, including for brokers and insurers.

items.headline: Insurance agents flag high hospital bills and inflated motor repair costs
items.summary: Insurance agents say high hospital bills and inflated motor repair costs are contributing to rising premiums.
items.detail: The comments point to medical cost inflation as a pressure on premiums. Such trends matter for pricing and for customers choosing cover.
items.why_it_matters: Rising hospital costs are the core pricing pressure in medical insurance, so this is useful context for IPMI pricing discussions.

items.headline: Air India cancels Riyadh and Dammam flights until November 7
items.summary: Air India and Air India Express have extended cancellations of Riyadh and Dammam flights until November 7 amid regional tensions.
items.detail: Riyadh Airport has separately announced the resumption of flights. The cancellations follow the recent missile and drone attacks in the region.
items.why_it_matters: If you travel between Dubai, Saudi Arabia and India, check your bookings, since schedules in the region are shifting.

items.headline: Emirates adds Airbus A350 on Kolkata-Dubai route, raising weekly flights to 12
items.summary: Emirates has put an Airbus A350 on the Kolkata-Dubai route, raising weekly flights to 12.
items.detail: The added capacity is aimed at travellers between eastern India and the UAE. The airline has already started operating the A350 on this route.
items.why_it_matters: More Emirates capacity to India can make travel home easier and may help with fares over time.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty fall for fourth straight session
items.summary: Indian markets closed lower for the fourth consecutive session, with the Nifty ending below 22,450.
items.detail: The Nifty fell nearly 2% over the week and is down about 13.6% year to date. Analysts cite rising energy prices, volatile global bond yields and geopolitical risk.
items.why_it_matters: Your Indian equity holdings and rupee savings are both sensitive to these moves, so this trend is worth watching.

items.headline: Rupee at 94.78 as IMF urges free movement and FIIs pull out
items.summary: The rupee gained 3 paise to 94.78 against the dollar, while the IMF has urged India to let it move freely.
items.detail: Foreign institutional investors have pulled out heavily in 2026, with outflows reported at Rs 3 trillion so far. Commentators say RBI measures are short-term stabilisers rather than a lasting fix.
items.why_it_matters: A weak rupee gives more dirhams worth of rupees when you send money home, but the rate is volatile, so timing matters.

items.headline: Crude surges past $110 as US-Iran tensions weigh on Indian markets
items.summary: Crude oil has risen above $110 a barrel, and markets have fallen for a third straight session on US-Iran tensions.
items.detail: Headlines link the move to the risk of further strikes around Iran. The global Fed meeting this week is also on investors' radar.
items.why_it_matters: Higher crude feeds into India's import bill and the rupee, and affects fuel and travel costs in the UAE.

items.headline: Who was Bibha Chowdhuri, the Indian physicist who studied cosmic rays?
items.summary: A profile of Bibha Chowdhuri, an Indian physicist who studied cosmic rays, has highlighted her legacy.
items.detail: She is remembered for her cosmic-ray research and was honoured with a star named after her. Her story is a useful reminder of India's early contributions to physics.

items.headline: Arctic ice had been expanding for at least 1,000 years before about 1960
items.summary: New research suggests Arctic ice was growing for at least a thousand years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960.
items.detail: The study frames that long expansion as a background trend that was reversed by global warming. It adds long-term context to today's climate debates.

items.headline: IIT Madras researcher joins study on a helical molecule that works as a single-molecule machine
items.summary: An IIT Madras faculty member contributed key input to a global study on molecular electronics.
items.detail: The study describes a helical molecule between gold electrodes that acts as a motor driven by electric current. The work is basic research, with possible future uses in tiny electronic devices.
